Research_Article_1_Description: Mapping between volumetric (e.g., MNI152) and surface (e.g., fsaverage) coordinate systems is crucial for neuroimaging, but methods for accurate transformations are underexplored. Description: A longitudinal study based in Brazil aiming to understand the development of mental disorders in children and adolescents.
Research_Article_1_Title: Estimated Prevalence of Depressive Disorders in Children From 2004 to 2019 A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Research_Article_1_Description: Depression during childhood (ie, age <13 years) poses a major health burden. Recent changes in environmental and lifestyle factors may increase children’s risk of mental health problems. This has been reported for anxiety disorders, but it is unclear whether this occurs for depressive disorders.
Research_Article_2_Title: Early Adversity and Development: Parsing Heterogeneity and Identifying Pathways of Risk and Resilience
Research_Article_2_Description: This research highlights how distinct adversity types (threat vs. deprivation) during development differentially impact psychopathology-threat affecting emotional processing via attention biases and genetic markers (e.g., *NR3C1*), while deprivation disrupts executive function through cortical-striatal circuits. Longitudinal data and multi-modal assessments revealed outcome heterogeneity tied to adversity timing, type, and protective factors, informing targeted intervention strategies.

Description: The BrainLat Project is a comprehensive, open-access neuroimaging dataset developed by the Latin American Brain Health Institute to advance research on neurodegenerative diseases within underrepresented populations. It encompasses multimodal data from 780 participants across five Latin American countries: Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.​
Research_Article_1_Title: Brain clocks capture diversity and disparities in aging and dementia across geographically diverse populations
Research_Article_1_Description: Region-specific analysis of accelerated brain aging by providing multimodal neuroimaging (fMRI/EEG) and clinical data from underrepresented Latin American populations, capturing structural inequality’s impact via frontoposterior network disruptions and sex-specific gaps linked to macrosocial stressors. Its inclusion of diverse sociodemographic, environmental, and genetic admixture profiles supported models where socioeconomic disparities and pollution explained 37% of variance in brain-age gaps, highlighting Global South vulnerabilities to accelerated neurodegeneration
Research_Article_2_Title: Altered spatiotemporal brain dynamics of interoception in behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia
Research_Article_2_Description: The study revealed that behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients exhibit prolonged intrinsic neural timescales during interoception, measured via EEG autocorrelation windows, linking these dynamic deficits to structural atrophy in fronto-insular-temporal regions and sociocognitive impairments. Multimodal data-including simultaneous EEG/ECG, structural MRI, and neuropsychological assessments-enabled mapping of spatiotemporal brain dynamics to allostatic-interoceptive network degradation, establishing a mechanistic basis for bvFTD’s behavioral symptoms
